claim: To select vertices/edges 'through' a mesh in Edit Mode from an orthographic view (e.g. box-selecting a duplicated detail's back-side points without rotating the view), enable the mesh tool option often called 'Occlude' / x-ray toggle (Alt+Z) so box-select picks up points regardless of whether they're facing the camera, instead of only the front-facing ones.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote: "with machine tools we're going to enable something called occlude it's the same same one as in here called x-ray mode... if you enable this you can actually see through mesh in edit mode... if you don't have this enabled and you're gonna try to select this in orthographic mode you select only objects i mean vertices that are visible to you which means the front ones"

claim: A Bevel modifier width sized for the object's overall scale will overshoot and mangle geometry when applied to a small cut/panel/array element -- it creates tangled, dense edge connections converging on single corner points. The fix is to manually reduce that Bevel modifier's width to match the scale of the specific small detail (the creator repeatedly dialed large default bevel widths down to about 0.2, and down to ~0.001 for very small keypad-button bevels).
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (~8:53-10:13): "this is going to be caused by the bevel see bevel is so large in here that simply overshoots these these cuts in addition to this uh probably blender creates some crazy connections you can see the pool on this side i bet you there's a massive amount of lines edges connecting each of these to one of these corner points which is insane... the problem here is the bevel is still too big using overshooting here so we need to grab this panel right this long panel and we need to change the bevel size... put a number in here like maybe 0.2"
rejected_alternative: Leaving the same bevel width used on the main body applied to small secondary/tertiary detail cuts
reason: A bevel width appropriate for the main body's scale is far too large relative to a small panel or array element, causing the bevel geometry to overshoot the cut and generate broken/overlapping edge connections; the width must be re-tuned per detail scale.

claim: The Mirror modifier mirrors around the object's origin point, not a visual centerline -- if an object's origin was relocated earlier in the workflow (e.g. after using P > Selection to separate a boolean cutter, which leaves the origin at the original parent object's location), a naively-added Mirror modifier folds/mirrors the piece onto itself instead of mirroring it outward to the opposite side. Fix: reset the origin to the object's own geometry (Object > Set Origin > Origin to Geometry) before mirroring, or explicitly target/bisect across the correct axis object.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (~10:54-11:14): "now there is a mirror here but from some reason doesn't work and it doesn't work before because we move the original point to the object now you can see that it's get mirrored across itself the mirror point by the default is the original point so what we need to do is instead of doing that turn off this y-axis for bisect select this thing and copy it across the main object"

claim: For a row of repeated boolean-cut details (rivets, vents, grille slats), add an Array modifier to the single cutter object set along the relevant axis to generate the repeats, rather than manually duplicating the cutter -- then apply/boolean-cut the array result into the target mesh.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (~24:15-24:17): "but we're going to array this so let's erade this um and array this on y axis first right here and then we need another array"
rejected_alternative: Manually shift-duplicating the cutter object N times along the axis

claim: Deliberately breaking perfect symmetry/centering in secondary detail placement (e.g. offsetting a keypad instead of centering it, sizing panels/vents unevenly on each side) tends to read as more visually interesting and believable than perfectly centered, uniform placement.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (~20:42): "let's make it longer and let's listen don't make it in the middle don't put it in the middle exactly it's going to be boring let's misalign it somewhere here it's going to be fun"; matches the earlier stated intent to create a 'larger panel and a small vent' in 'a non-symmetrical fashion' near the start of the video.
reason: Perfectly centered, uniform secondary details were judged 'boring' by the creator; asymmetric placement was chosen for visual interest.
